title: Harper Launches 5.0: Fully Open-Source Runtime for Building and Deploying Cost-Efficient Agents
partialText: Harper 5.0 makes its core fully open source under Apache 2.0, adds RocksDB alongside LMDB, and doubles down on its unified runtime for agentic engineering. By combining database, cache, messaging, and logic into a single process, it reduces latency and simplifies deployment. Built for AI-driven development, it enables faster, cheaper, and more scalable applications.

title: Designing Reliable App Switch Flows on iOS for Secure Transactions
partialText: App Switch architecture on iOS allows one app to hand off execution to another and resume the flow through callbacks, but reliable implementation requires treating the interaction as a distributed transaction rather than simple navigation. Strong state management, secure deep linking using Universal Links, strict callback validation, and backend verification are critical to prevent failures and security issues. Observability and transaction-level tracking further enable performance optimization and production reliability.

title: Why LLMs Alone Can't Migrate Your Legacy Code, and What I Built Instead
partialText: A new system automates the migration of legacy SAS scripts to PySpark for enterprise clients. The system was built with deterministic parsing to understand the source code. Structured pattern extraction to capture business-critical data. Validation pipelines to catch what the LLM gets wrong.

title: What It Really Means to Be Cloud-Native: A Practical Checklist

title: Why Your AI Agent Keeps Forgetting (Even With 1M Tokens)
partialText: This article argues that large context windows are not a substitute for proper memory in AI agents. Instead, effective systems rely on layered memory architectures—working, session, condensed, durable, and retrieval memory—to manage context growth, reduce cost, and improve accuracy. By focusing on memory lifecycle design rather than raw context size, developers can build more reliable, scalable agents that avoid common failures like repetition, context drift, and missed recall.

title: Your AI-Generated Code Tests Might Be Lying to You
partialText: You know code coverage helps you see what code is running. But with mutation tests, you get to see what your tests are actually capable of catching. An AI-written code will pass any code coverage tool with ease, but 15-25% more code will pass a mutation test, indicating your tests are not as good as they look on a code coverage report.

partialText: Cayuse integrates PlayerZero across its 20+ apps to proactively identify and fix issues before they reach customers. title: Moth Delusion
partialText: A brilliant entomologist, Hapley, locked in a lifelong rivalry with Pawkins, becomes psychologically destabilized while studying moths. After Pawkins dies, Hapley's obsessive conflict finds a new target in an unknown moth that appears to only he can see. The insect becomes a projection of rivalry and obsession, driving him into violence and hallucination, ending in confinement.

title: Azuma-zi’s Machine Cult
partialText: In a Camberwell dynamo shed, Holroyd, a violent electrician, and Azuma-zi, an immigrant stoker, work amid roaring machines. Azuma-zi worships the largest dynamo as a living god, reading its noises as divine will. After abuse by Holroyd, he believes sacrifice is demanded. The machine kills Holroyd in an accident. Azuma-zi attacks a manager and dies by electrocution, ending the cult of machine worship in London.

title: Eyes That Wandered Beyond Space
partialText: After a lightning strike in a laboratory, Sidney Davidson loses normal sight and instead sees a remote island thousands of miles away in real time. Blind to his surroundings, he experiences another world overlapping reality. Weeks later he recovers—but evidence proves his visions were real, hinting at a terrifying possibility: sight can exist independent of the body across space.

title: Market Timing & Relevance: The Factor You Can't Fully Control
partialText:
Market timing receives 10% weight in Proof of Usefulness scoring — the second-lowest weighting in the framework. This is a deliberate choice that reflects a specific analytical judgment: timing is real, consequential, and mostly outside founder control.

Penalizing teams heavily for factors they cannot meaningfully influence would make the framework less honest, not more rigorous. The 10% weight acknowledges timing without allowing it to dominate an evaluation that should primarily measure what teams actually built and whether it actually works.
